content.text:
I reviewed every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all four figure briefs, and built a full source ledger tracing each claim limitation, numbered part, and figure statement to the disclosure.

Key traces I confirmed:

- **Claim 1 / 11 core**: branch limit below sum of ratings, per-channel contactor + connector current sensor + control-pilot interface + local connector identifier, upstream branch current sensor, stored authorization/requested current/minimum sustaining current/energy-deficit value, per-interval subtraction of measured non-charging branch load and configurable safety reserve, sustaining-first then deficit distribution, pilot send + connector verification, reduced pilot command, and verification-interval-gated one-at-a-time ordered shedding — all match disclosure ¶1–3 nearly verbatim. "Remains above the branch limit **after** a reduced pilot command" entails the pre-command over-limit condition recited in claim 1's reduced-command trigger.
- **Dependents**: claim 2 (re-measure after each opening, stop early) follows from "one at a time … **until** measured branch current is below the branch limit"; claims 3/13, 4/14, 5, 6–8/15, 9–10/16 each map to disclosure ¶3–5.
- **Figures**: FIG. 1 topology (parallel drops downstream of a branch sensor that reads total current, bus reaching only the two connector channels, separate sensing link to the controller) is consistent with "measures total current upstream of the connector contactors" and "communicates with the connector interfaces and contactors over an isolated local bus" — the bus's enumerated membership is what licenses excluding the non-charging load and routing the connector-sensor read separately. FIG. 2's contactor-then-sensor-then-connector order is required by welded-contactor detection (sensor must read current after an open command). FIG. 3's sub-blocks and outboard fault indicator, and FIG. 4's eight shapes with the two return paths and the welded-branch terminator, match the described steps 202–216 one-for-one.
- **Depiction conventions**: the schematic housings, dashed enclosures, square/circle sensor and contactor outlines, and equal-size blocks are shape-neutral generic outlines confined to the figure briefs; the application text and Brief Description never verbalize a shape, never say "by way of example", and add no undisclosed geometry, position, or contact relationship.
- **Internal checks**: all 25 numerals appear in both the briefs and the description with a single meaning each; leader targets match the described geometry; step names in `draft/numerals.md`, FIG. 4, and the description are identical; no section lines exist to cross-check; no placeholders, drafting notes, or unresolved alternatives remain; formalities (no priority claim, no government support, no means-plus-function, apparatus + method classes, abstract ≈146 words) are consistent with the brief.

No untraced technical assertion surfaced, so I am returning an empty findings array.

input.summary: Full ledger built and closed with no findings. I traced every limitation of all sixteen claims (1-10 apparatus, 11-16 method), every one of the twenty-five numerals in draft/numerals.md, every numbered part and relationship in the detailed description, all four figure briefs, the Brief Description of the Drawings, the Summary, the Abstract, and the title/cross-reference/government-support formalities, against affirmative USER text in input/disclosure.md (the conversation.md USER passage is a truncated duplicate of disclosure paragraphs 1-3 and adds nothing further; input/brief.md was used only for the no-priority and no-federal-support statements). Core independent-claim matter maps almost verbatim to disclosure paragraphs 1-3: branch limit lower than the sum of connector ratings; per-channel contactor, connector current sensor, control-pilot interface and local connector identifier; branch current sensor upstream of the connector contactors; stored charging authorization, requested current, minimum sustaining current and energy-deficit value; per-interval subtraction of measured non-charging branch load and configurable safety reserve; sustaining-current-first then energy-deficit distribution; pilot transmission with connector-sensor verification; reduced pilot command; and verification-interval-gated opening of contactors one at a time in a stored shedding order until measured branch current is below the branch limit. The reduced-pilot trigger recited in claims 1 and 11 is entailed by "remains above the branch limit after a reduced pilot command," which presupposes the pre-command over-limit condition. Claims 2 and 12 (re-measurement after each opening, opening no further contactor) follow from "one at a time ... until measured branch current is below the branch limit." Claims 3/13, 4/14, 5, 6/15, 7, 8, 9/16 and 10 trace respectively to the three reclosure conditions, the leakage-threshold welded condition with inhibition of the other contactors on the branch and local fault indicator, the isolated local bus to connector interfaces and contactors, the signed local token plus last accepted branch limit in nonvolatile memory with outage continuation, the expiry-and-identifier gate on new sessions, the tamper-evident meter sequence uploaded on return of communication, and the service-input mapping by one low-energy pilot transition at a time stored only after the sensed channel agrees. Figure geometry was checked for functional substance rather than accepted as generic: FIG. 1's placement of the branch current sensor upstream of all three parallel drops matches "measures total current"; the bus reaching only the two connector channels and not the non-charging load matches the disclosure's enumeration of what the bus carries; FIG. 2's contactor-then-connector-current-sensor-then-vehicle-connector order is required by welded-contactor detection after an open command; FIG. 3's network interface, nonvolatile memory, service input and outboard local fault indicator match the disclosed controller elements; FIG. 4's eight shapes, two return paths and welded-branch terminator match steps 202 through 216 exactly. Remaining visual choices (dashed grouping rectangles, empty rectangles, the small square contactor outline, the small circle sensor outline, the rounded vehicle outline, equal block sizes, in-page placement of sub-blocks) are shape-neutral depiction conventions confined to the figure briefs; the application text and Brief Description verbalize no shape, no proportion, no "by way of example" outline, and no undisclosed position, contact or flow relationship, and no optional embodiment was added to justify a renderer choice. Internal consistency verified: each numeral carries one meaning across FIG. 1, FIG. 2, FIG. 3, FIG. 4, the ledger and the description; leader targets agree with the described line work; the step names 202-216 are identical in the ledger, the FIG. 4 brief and the description; claim and description terminology agree (connector channel, assigned current limit, stored shedding order, verification interval, reduced pilot command, leakage threshold, randomized recovery delay, signed local authorization token, last accepted branch limit, tamper-evident local sequence, low-energy pilot transition, configurable safety reserve); no section lines exist requiring designation matching; and no drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction, unresolved alternative or internal comment remains anywhere in the draft or briefs. Background prior-art characterizations were not treated as requiring inventor support. Formalities are consistent with the brief: no priority claim, no federally sponsored research, apparatus and method statutory classes, a graduated dependent-claim ladder, no means-plus-function language, and an abstract of roughly 146 words.

input.summary:
Full ledger built and traced; no unsupported or inconsistent item found, so findings is empty.

Scope checked: input/disclosure.md and the single USER passage in input/conversation.md as the only invention authority (the conversation transcript truncates mid-sentence at "through a network interface, but", but disclosure.md carries the complete offline-authorization, tamper-evident-record and service-input text, so nothing in the draft rests on the truncated remainder); input/brief.md used only for formalities (no priority claim -> "Not applicable" cross-reference; no federally sponsored R&D -> "Not applicable" government-support statement; apparatus + method statutory classes; no means-plus-function language; graduated dependent ladder — all satisfied).

Claims: all 16 traced limitation by limitation. Claim 1 structure (contactor between branch and respective connector, connector current sensor, control-pilot interface, local connector identifier, upstream branch current sensor, controller coupled to all four) matches "Each connector has a controllable contactor, a connector current sensor, a control-pilot interface, and a local connector identifier" and "A branch current sensor measures total current upstream of the connector contactors." The allocation limitation matches "subtracts measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch limit... first assigns the minimum sustaining current to sessions that can receive it, then distributes remaining current according to energy deficit... sends each assigned limit through the control-pilot interface and verifies the resulting connector current." The reduced-pilot-command and verification-interval shedding limitations match "If measured branch current remains above the branch limit after a reduced pilot command for a verification interval, the controller opens connector contactors one at a time in a stored shedding order until measured branch current is below the branch limit"; the pilot-reduction trigger is the necessary antecedent of that disclosed conditional and of "staged reduction followed by ordered contactor shedding when branch current does not respond." Claims 2/12 (re-measure after each opening, open no further contactor) rest on "until measured branch current is below the branch limit." Claims 3/13 (zero connector current, connected-vehicle report, randomized recovery delay), 4/14 (leakage threshold, inhibit other contactors on the branch, local fault indicator), 5 (isolated local bus to interfaces and contactors), 6/7/15 (network interface, signed local token and last accepted branch limit in nonvolatile memory, continued authorized sessions, no new session absent an unexpired token naming that connector), 8 (tamper-evident sequence uploaded on return), and 9/10/16 (service input, one low-energy pilot transition at a time, store only after the sensed channel agrees) each map to an exact disclosure sentence. Antecedent basis and terminology are consistent between claims, summary, description and abstract; the abstract is ~140 words.

Numerals: all 25 ledger entries (100–140, 202–216) appear in the description and in exactly one figure each with one meaning apiece; no numeral is used for two parts and no described part lacks its ledger entry. Every part corresponds to a disclosed element or a disclosed operation (charging installation, branch conductor, branch current sensor, edge controller, isolated local bus, network interface, nonvolatile memory, service input, local fault indicator, non-charging load implied by "measured non-charging branch load", two connector channels, contactor, connector current sensor, control-pilot interface, vehicle connector, connected electric vehicle, and the eight process steps).

Figure briefs: FIG. 1–3 use only generic empty rectangles, a square, a circle and a rounded rectangle, all called schematic, with claims and description shape-neutral; no proportion, count, material, taper, depth, runout or contact-topology statement conveys undisclosed technical substance. The topology statements that are substantive are all traced: branch sensor upstream of all three taps ("measures total current"), contactor upstream of the connector current sensor (required by "not reclosed until its connector current sensor reports zero"), bus reaching only the contactor and control-pilot interface (the disclosure lists exactly "the connector interfaces and contactors" on the bus), sensor-reading coupling shown separately and left free-ended, and the local fault indicator outside the controller but driven by it. FIG. 4's eight shapes, arrow chain, the 210 return path, the 214 welded branch to a terminator, and the 216 return path match the described flow and the four flow-diagram numeral names. No "by way of example", "any closed outline", or shape-justifying language appears anywhere in the application text; the Brief Description entries match the briefs and no section lines exist to cross-check. No drafting note, placeholder, open question, unresolved alternative or internal comment remains in any draft section.
